This series begins with super-droplet representation, then moves through seeded-particle properties, background aerosol environments, and a κ–radius–timing response surface, before turning to updraft–timing regimes, terminal-velocity sensitivity, and a paper replication. Every note separates the question, baseline, changed conditions, diagnostics, limitations, and next hypothesis.

::: {.callout-note title="Relationship to PySDM-Seeding-Lab"}
All experiments below were run independently on the **laboratory server with Visual Studio Code**, not through the PySDM-Seeding-Lab app. Experiments 1–4 are precursor studies that informed the Lab's experiment and validation design; Experiments 5–7 are script-based follow-up studies carried out after the Lab was built.
:::

## Experiment sequence

```text
Experiment 1  numerical representation and ensemble stability
      ↓
Experiment 2  dry radius · κ · timing sensitivity and growth pathway
      ↓
Experiment 3  background aerosol · fixed-number/mass comparison
      ↓
Experiment 4  activation-strength · timing response surface
      ↓
Experiment 5  updraft × injection-timing regimes that set the sign of the response
      ↓
Experiment 6  sensitivity of the conclusions to the terminal-velocity formula
      ↓
Experiment 7  0-D parcel replication of the Ren et al. (2025) particle-size experiment
```
